findings.failure_scenario: An agent JSON whose eternalai config contains only "model" (valid, since validate_config requires only "model") calls generate_text: `chain_id or self.config["chain_id"]` raises KeyError('chain_id'), which the outer handler converts to EternalAIError('Text generation failed: chain_id'). The fallback `if not chain_id: chain_id = "45762"` two lines below is unreachable, so the default the PR adds for exactly this case never runs and text generation is broken for all such configs.
findings.summary: Reading self.config["chain_id"] with [] raises KeyError before the newly added "45762" default can ever apply, so any config without chain_id fails every generate_text call.

findings.failure_scenario: The chat API call succeeds and returns text, but the response body has no onchain_data (e.g. EternalAI_API_URL points at any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which configure() explicitly permits by prompting for an arbitrary URL, or the API omits the field). The `if completion.onchain_data is not None` check raises AttributeError, the `except:` branch then evaluates the same attribute again in the f-string, the second AttributeError escapes the inner handler, and the outer except raises EternalAIAPIError('Text generation failed: ...object has no attribute onchain_data'). ConnectionManager logs the error and returns None, so prompt_llm gets None and post_tweet silently never posts.
findings.summary: The bare-except fallback re-reads completion.onchain_data, so any successful response that lacks that field is converted into an EternalAIError instead of returning the generated text.

findings.failure_scenario: A response whose choices array is empty passes the None check and line 165 raises IndexError on choices[0]; likewise a response where message.content is None (refusal or content-less completion) returns None to the caller and the tweet is silently dropped. The added check provides false assurance against neither of the failures it appears to guard.
findings.summary: The new `completion.choices is None` guard is dead code — the SDK always deserializes choices to a list — while the real failure modes (empty choices, None content) stay unguarded.

findings.failure_scenario: list-actions and Action.validate_params never learn about chain_id, and ConnectionManager.perform_action rejects any call whose params length differs from the required count (2), so chain_id can never be supplied through the action system — the only functional source is the config dict. The public parameter misleads callers into passing an argument the framework cannot deliver.
findings.summary: The new chain_id parameter of generate_text is not declared in the "generate-text" Action's parameter list, so it is invisible to the action framework and unreachable through it.

findings.failure_scenario: Maintenance cost: the `chain_id == ""` clause can never change the branch outcome (empty string, None, and 0 are all falsy and already caught by `not chain_id`), so readers must determine it is dead rather than meaningful; the redundant clause sits inside the defaulting logic that is itself broken by the KeyError raised at line 144.
findings.summary: The condition `if not chain_id or chain_id == "":` is redundant — `not ""` is already True — so the second operand is dead code.
